findings.description: The sealed baseline turns the repository architecture gate red. crates/core/Cargo.toml adds serde_json (correct and required by C4's BTreeMap<String,serde_json::Value> and named by C12), but crates/testkit/src/bin/unisphere-arch-check.rs:15 still allows only 'serde' for unisphere-core, so against real cargo metadata the binary errors 'forbidden normal dependency: unisphere-core -> serde_json' and exits FAILURE. .harness/extensions/checks/checks.mjs:85 runs that exact binary with no --metadata as the 'architecture' gate, so harness checks is red at 3df24503. C12 explicitly required dependency checks to be updated to the actual approved graph in this same change. The recorded proof missed it because vd-0001 ran only 'cargo test -p unisphere-core -p unisphere-testkit --lib' plus scoped clippy, and the binary's own unit tests read fixtures/architecture/allowed.json whose unisphere-core package also lists only serde - sensor and fixture drifted together. Ownership makes it worse: crates/testkit/src/bin/** and fixtures/architecture/** belong to tk-0005 (pm, wave 2), and tk-0002/tk-0003/tk-0004 list them in neither paths nor reads, so all three wave-1 lanes would inherit a red gate on a file none of them may edit. Fix before seal: allow matches!(dependency, "serde" | "serde_json") for core, add the edge to allowed.json and bump the expected count 7->8, then run the architecture gate itself rather than the scoped --lib tests. Separately for wave-1 planning, check() also rejects workspace members outside its hardcoded five-name list at lines 54-61, so the same wave-2 file must gain the three new package names and their C12 edges the moment those crates appear.

findings.description: The frozen conformance helper asserts three of the four properties C13 names. assert_adapter_conformance (crates/testkit/src/collection.rs:252-316) covers determinism, source-provenance and content policy well, but nothing about outputbounds, and MAX_OUTPUT_BATCH_BYTES appears nowhere in testkit. Because the helper is frozen at wave 0 and tk-0003/tk-0004 list crates/testkit/src/collection.rs under reads rather than paths, no lane can add the assertion later without breaching the fence, so every adapter that 'passes conformance' will have passed a check silent about the bound the writer must enforce. Implementable now with what the crate already has: TelemetryRecord is Serialize and testkit already depends on serde_json. Related decision worth making explicit rather than leaving implicit: the fixtures carry SENSITIVE-* markers precisely so leakage is mechanically detectable, yet the shared helper never scans a metadata-only mapping for them; leaving that to each lane's own tests is defensible but should be stated.
findings.evidence: crates/testkit/src/collection.rs:252-316; guide C13; guide C9 MAX_OUTPUT_BATCH_BYTES; units tk-0003/tk-0004 reads

findings.description: 'Blank line' is defined twice and not identically. C3 says blank lines consume budget and cursor but are omitted from returned records; fixture_records at crates/testkit/src/collection.rs:23 implements blank as line.iter().all(u8::is_ascii_whitespace), and fixture_framing_preserves_physical_offsets_across_blanks_and_crlf pins that reading with a space-only first line. A tk-0002 author could just as reasonably implement blank as an empty physical line, after which the real loader returns a whitespace-only NativeRecord the fixture path never produces - adapter tests stay green while the live pipeline emits diagnostics for a record shape never exercised. Pin the definition in C3 or the helper doc comment before the lanes diverge.

CollectionApi object safety is claimed in C1 and consumed as &dyn CollectionApi by C11, but never exercised through dyn at baseline; the FakeCollector test calls through the concrete type. Verified dyn-compatible by inspection (both methods take &self, neither is generic, neither returns Self, Send+Sync supertraits are fine), so risk is low - but SessionAdapter is compile-proven because assert_adapter_conformance takes &dyn SessionAdapter, and CollectionApi deserves the same. Adding 'let _: &dyn CollectionApi = &fake;' to the existing test converts a stated property into a compile-time one at wave 0 inside a file tk-0001 already owns, rather than first testing it in wave 2 when the CLI depends on it.

Two pre-seeded false positives for the C13 source scan, recorded so tk-0005 does not build a sensor that fails on correct code: crates/core/src/lib.rs:4 is #![forbid(unsafe_code)], so a naive 'unsafe' denylist term flags the exact attribute that establishes the property; and crates/testkit/src/collection.rs:10-11 legitimately uses include_bytes! for fixtures, so the enumerated production file list must exclude testkit rather than sweeping the repo. A denylist scan of the five committed core production sources for std::{fs,env,process,net,thread}, SystemTime/Instant::now, unsafe, extern " and include_str!/include_bytes! returned zero hits outside that one forbid attribute - core is clean.
